A.summary: A planner picks one of three tiers: exact haloed tiles when the summed reach fits, an exact whole-image streaming pass with a (2R+1) ring buffer working in place in the output, or stages separated by reduced-resolution fields. Each stage evaluates a tile by propagating regions of interest backwards through its ops, and a wide blur can be split into a truncated local Gaussian plus a residual field.

The tiers are documented well (impl-A/src/index.ts:344-355), but buildField is a 136-line dense accumulator with corner and edge special cases (impl-A/src/index.ts:567-703), blurRects takes 11 positional parameters (impl-A/src/index.ts:173-185), and the planner's thresholds are magic numbers. change_requests.notes: Exact tiles are easy because every InternOp carries R and evalStage propagates rects generically. The 'blur' kind checks in the planner, the stage compiler and the streaming tier all need a new branch. A wide sharpen cannot become a field, because the stage after the field has lost v.

Of the six, A's backward ROI propagation is the closest seam to a resampling op (inputRectFor(outputRect) per op). But W/H are global in Env, the output is allocated at input size, and streaming and fields assume a single frame.

F.summary: renderTiled walks the compiled ops and accumulates a pending local segment while its reach fits floor((sqrt(budget)-1)/2). A blur that does not fit is either streamed exactly in full-width strips (if it is the last blur) or turned into a field: an anti-alias pre-blur, a box downsample with a ring of clamped edge cells, and a residual sigma, coarsened until its kernel can be haloed. The final segment is tiled from the current source on a grid chosen to minimise reads.

change_requests.notes: Nearly local on the exact path: a new PxOp kind, a branch in applySegment, and the reach in sumReach and the loop. A wide sharpen does not fit, because the field replaces src and v is gone, and renderStreamed is blur-only.
The Source abstraction (image or field sampled by frame coordinates) is a good seam for a different grid, but applySegment clips to img.width/height and the output is allocated at W×H.

F.tests_as_laws: Mostly examples, with a few honest-contract checks. There is a reference implementation, but it mirrors the implementation's half-kernel formulation (impl-F/test/render.test.ts:30-74). Read rectangles must contain the written rect (impl-F/test/render.test.ts:209-225), and the streamed path must emit many strips (impl-F/test/render.test.ts:435-448). The whole-frame route covers the 'wide short frame' trap (impl-F/test/render.test.ts:464-479), but there are no negative controls.

cross.generativity: Yes, largely. Every implementation compiles sigmaUm to pixels once, sums radii along the chain into the halo, evaluates a tile from its read rectangle, and has one fallback for kernels that do not fit. A, B, D and F converged on the same participants (local segment with summed reach, per-blur global field sampled bilinearly by frame coordinates, variance-corrected residual), each different in detail: A's cell grid spanning the domain, B's chunked power-of-two field, D's exact tail corrections, F's padded ring with a pre-blur. Independently, A, E and F each found an exact path that streams with small buffers instead of tiling (ring buffers in the output, or full-width strips). E replaced the field with an exact interior/strip/corner decomposition, and C collapsed the whole thing to one global switch.
cross.worse_is_better: Partly. C is the smallest (660 lines) and the most habitable. Its single switch (exact tiles, or the whole chain on one padded reduced image) meets the task's stated tolerances in its tests, which suggests the chapter's per-kernel local/global strategy is more than this task's contract demands. But C pays where it counts: in a mixed chain the narrow blurs and interior gammas are also approximated, and the wide path does not tile. The per-kernel split of B/D/F is the better design for mixed chains, so the yardstick is not over-asking on that point. It over-asks on alignment, power-of-two tiles and refusal.
ideas_the_yardstick_lacks: choose the tile grid by minimising total reads sum(readW·readH), with balanced counts to avoid slivers, instead of the largest power of two (impl-C/src/index.ts:259, impl-E/src/index.ts:856, impl-F/src/index.ts:249)

an exact streaming path that needs no halo: separable passes with (2R+1) ring buffers in place in the exempt output (impl-A/src/index.ts:716, impl-E/src/index.ts:725), or full-width strips for the vertical pass (impl-F/src/index.ts:589)

clamped borders dominate the field error for wide kernels: exact edge-line or tail-mass corrections (impl-A/src/index.ts:583-693, impl-D/src/index.ts:309-336, impl-E/src/index.ts:292-310) or a padded ring of clamped edge values (impl-B/src/index.ts:510, impl-C/src/index.ts:448-457, impl-F/src/index.ts:103-109)
split a wide Gaussian into a truncated local part plus a residual-variance field, using additivity of variances (impl-A/src/index.ts:877-886)
an anti-alias pre-blur before decimation, counted in the variance budget (impl-C/src/index.ts:463-466, impl-F/src/index.ts:318-321)
a cost model that pushes exact-capable but too-expensive plans to fields (impl-B/src/index.ts:378-398, impl-D/src/index.ts:559-584)
store a field larger than one buffer in budget-sized chunks (impl-B/src/index.ts:179-199)
a whole-frame route when the image fits the budget, even if no tile could carry the halo (impl-F/src/index.ts:703-711, impl-B/src/index.ts:320-328)
yardstick_problems: 'refuse with a diagnostic' contradicts requirement 3 (must still complete); no implementation refuses, and D reuses the T/4 rule as a classification threshold instead (impl-D/src/index.ts:615-618)
rounding the halo up to a multiple of 8 and adding 1 px for bilinear safety is GPU-specific and would raise reads against the 3× limit for small budgets; nobody does it
'largest power-of-two tile fitting half the budget' wastes half of maxTilePixels and increases reads; implementations use the full budget and read-minimising grids

a power-of-two downsample is not needed on CPU; E and C pick the finest integer scale that fits (impl-E/src/index.ts:338-349, impl-C/src/index.ts:461), and F tries 1..64 first (impl-F/src/index.ts:344)
fields replace the source of later stages, so the chapter's structure cannot express an op that needs both its neighbourhood and its own centre value (change request 1)
the chapter assumes one frame per evaluation; a grid-changing op (change request 2) needs demand-driven region mapping, which the chapter lists only as a variation
